input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement on written notice, with service continuing only to the last day of the month following the notice month - i.e. roughly 30 to 60 days' run-off. That is a Customer convenience right on notice no longer than the 60-90 day fallback window (and close to the 30-day preferred standard), and it is unconditional, so no cause or Vendor consent is needed. No early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated minimum payment is imposed on that election anywhere in the Agreement, so the fallback three-month fee cap is satisfied by there being no fee at all. TrueLink has no mid-term convenience termination right: the only Vendor-side exit is the 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year period (p0078), which is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term and is a RENEWAL-rule item, not a T4C convenience right (the Section 2/3 cut-offs in p0078 are cause-based). The term is one year, not a multi-year commitment, so the walk-away test is not engaged. Two points short of preferred are noted rather than flagged: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (fees are invoiced monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt under p0045, so nothing is prepaid), and the run-off can exceed 30 days depending on the notice date. We also note that Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof" and Section 4 is not included in the text supplied; if Section 4 contains a minimum-commitment or accelerated-payment mechanic we would revisit. On the material terms visible, this clause sits at or above the fallback position and we would not redline it.
